title: Bounded injective model for derived coinduction
statement: Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Work in the ordinary module derived categories $D(A)$ and $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], using derived Hom on the one-object ringed sites [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $L\in D(A)$, let $a\leq b$ be integers, and let $I^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of injective $A$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions] with $I^q=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$ and an isomorphism $Q(I^\bullet)\cong L$. Let $C_f(L)\in D(B)$ be derived coinduction, namely $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B[0],L)$ with the action $(c\varphi)(x)=\varphi(xc)$ on a K-injective Hom representative. The complex $J^\bullet$ with $J^q=\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,I^q)$, differential $d_J^q(\varphi)=d_I^q\circ\varphi$, and action $(c\varphi)(x)=\varphi(xc)$ has injective $B$-module terms and $J^q=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. There is a canonical isomorphism $Q(J^\bullet)\cong C_f(L)$ in $D(B)$, whose restriction to $D(A)$ is the usual K-injective computation of $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B[0],L)$. No Noetherian, finite-map, flatness, or scalar-action-isomorphism assumption is made.

source.place: Tag 08XR, lemma-hom-injective, and Tag 0AX0, lemma-dualizing-finite, first proof paragraph (bounded coinduced injective model); Tag 0A70, lemma-right-adjoint, for the derived coinduction construction.

proof.text: Put $H(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,M)$ with $(c\varphi)(x)=\varphi(xc)$ and $H(v)(\varphi)=v\circ\varphi$. Associativity and the unit in $B$ give the module laws, and postcomposition is additive and $B$-linear. Applying this to $I$ gives exactly $J$: $d_J^2(\varphi)=d_I^2\circ\varphi=0$, and $d_J(c\varphi)(x)=d_I(\varphi(xc))=(c\,d_J\varphi)(x)$. Outside $[a,b]$, $I^q=0$ and hence $J^q=\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,0)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AX0, lemma-dualizing-finite, first proof paragraph: the degreewise Hom complex and its bounded support; action from the construction before Tag 0A70.

proof.text: For a $B$-module $N$ and an $A$-module $M$, evaluation at $1$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_B(N,H(M))$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_A(UN,M)$, where $U$ restricts scalars. Its inverse sends $g$ to $n\mapsto(x\mapsto g(xn))$; the two composites are identities since $\psi(xn)(1)=(x\psi(n))(1)=\psi(n)(x)$. These formulas commute with pre- and postcomposition. Thus $U\dashv H$. A monomorphism of modules is an injective underlying map, so restriction preserves monomorphisms. Apply [lem-exc-rg-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] with $F=U$, $G=H$ and each injective $I^q$: $J^q=H(I^q)$ is injective over $B$.

source.place: Tag 08XR, lemma-hom-injective and its proof; the invoked general adjoint criterion is homology.tex Tag 015Z, lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives.

proof.text: The hypothesis $I^q=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$ implies $I^q=0$ for $q<a$. Together with termwise injectivity this verifies both hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective] in the abelian category of $A$-modules. Consequently $I$ is K-injective.

Write $e:QI\cong L$. Choose the K-injective representative $T$ with $t:QT\cong L$ used to define $C_f(L)=QH(T)$ in [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], $t^{-1}e$ and $e^{-1}t$ lift uniquely to homotopy classes $u:I\to T$ and $v:T\to I$. The same bijection, now for target $I$ and target $T$, gives $vu\simeq1_I$ and $uv\simeq1_T$. Postcomposition by each component of these homotopies gives $B$-linear homotopies after $H$: the identity $vu-1=dh+hd$ becomes $H(v)H(u)-1=dH(h)+H(h)d$. Hence $QH(u):QJ\cong QH(T)=C_f(L)$ is an isomorphism in $D(B)$. The uniqueness of the lifted homotopy class makes this comparison independent of the lifts. For a further representative the comparison classes compose, since their images under $Q$ compose and the same bijection is injective; this proves canonicity relative to $e$.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, characterization (3); applied to the coinduction construction in dualizing.tex before Tag 0A70.

proof.text: On the one-object identity-cover $A$-ringed site, the Hom complex $\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(B[0],I)$ has only the $p=0$ factor in degree $q$, namely $\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,I^q)$, and its differential is $d_I\circ\varphi$ because $d_{B[0]}=0$. Thus it is precisely $UJ$. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and Step 3 this computes $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B[0],L)$. The restriction of Step 4 is postcomposition $\varphi\mapsto u\circ\varphi$ on this same Hom complex, so its comparison is the usual K-injective comparison, with no extra action or scalar normalization. All constructions used only the stated ring map and injectivity and support hypotheses.

lean.statement: theorem coinduction_bounded_injective_model {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B) [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} (ModuleCat.{u} A)] [HasDerivedCategory.{wB} (ModuleCat.{u} B)] (L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (a b : ℤ) (_hab : a ≤ b) (I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (hIinj : ∀ q : ℤ, Injective (I.X q)) (hIsupp : ∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q → IsZero (I.X q)) (s : DerivedCategory.Q.obj I ≅ L) : (∀ q : ℤ, Injective (((coinductionComplexFunctor f).obj I).X q)) ∧ (∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q → IsZero (((coinductionComplexFunctor f).obj I).X q)) ∧ ∃ (hI : I.IsKInjective) (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((coinductionComplexFunctor f).obj I) ≅ (derivedCoinduction f).obj L), e = (@derivedCoinductionModel A B _ _ f _ _ I hI).symm ≪≫ (derivedCoinduction f).mapIso s ∧ (restrictScalars f).mapDerivedCategory.map e.hom ≫ (derivedCoinductionUnderlyingComparison f).hom.app L = (restrictScalars f).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app ((coinductionComplexFunctor f).obj I) ≫ (@derivedCoinductionUnderlyingModel A B _ _ f _ I hI).inv ≫ (derivedCoinductionUnderlyingHom f).map s.hom
